deities: Small Hanuman idol at the base shrine (approx. 12 ft)

history.summary: The Paritala Anjaneya Temple is famous for its colossal concrete statue of Veera Abhaya Anjaneya (Hanuman), which at 135 feet (41 metres) was at installation in 2003 one of the tallest Hanuman statues in the world and entered the Limca Book of Records. The statue, installed on 22 June 2003, stands beside National Highway 65 at Paritala village in Kanchikacherla mandal, about 30 km from Vijayawada, and is a landmark visible to highway travellers. Though taller Hanuman statues have since been built elsewhere in India, the Paritala statue remains an iconic pilgrimage stop for Hanuman devotees. At its base stands the small Paritala Anjaneya Temple shrine, with additional shrines of Lord Rama and a smaller Hanuman idol, gardens and visitor facilities in the complex.

name: Paritala Anjaneya Temple
town_description: Paritala is a village in Kanchikacherla mandal of NTR district, Andhra Pradesh, about 30 km from Vijayawada on National Highway 65, with a 2011 census population of around 9,700. It is known almost entirely for the towering Hanuman statue that rises beside the highway, making it a popular stop for pilgrims and travellers between Vijayawada and Hyderabad. The village lies in the Krishna river basin and is administered by a gram panchayat.

travel.airport: Vijayawada International Airport (Gannavaram, approx. 51 km via NH-65; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Vijayawada Junction (approx. 30 km); the temple is a roadside stop on NH-65 towards Hyderabad.
travel.road: Directly on National Highway 65 (old NH-9) at Paritala village, Kanchikacherla mandal; approx. 30-32 km (about 45 min) from Vijayawada by road. APSRTC buses and private vehicles ply the Vijayawada-Hyderabad highway; ample parking at the temple complex.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Hanuman Jayanti is the most vibrant time to visit, though it draws large crowds. Visiting in daylight hours is best to appreciate the full scale of the statue.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daily 6:00 AM to 8:00 PM (verify - one source lists closing at 9:00 PM). Entry is free; photography of the statue is permitted in the outer areas, but check restrictions inside the inner shrines. Footwear not allowed inside; dress modestly.
